docs.title: pyramids-lazy
docs.text:
The lazy / dask compute backend for pyramids. pyramids-core ships the raster, cube and vector data model and every eager operation that follows from data already in hand; what it deliberately does not ship is the dask/zarr stack. This package is that stack, and nothing else.

Installing it alongside pyramids-core turns on every lazy operation — lazy raster and variable reads, lazy NetCDF cubes, to_dask_dataframe, kerchunk manifests, multi-file dask reads, Zarr read/write for Dataset and DatasetCollection, and lazy (dask-geopandas) vector reads — without dask, distributed, zarr or kerchunk ever being pulled into a bare pyramids-core install.

docs.title: No import required
docs.text:
There is no API here you call directly, and no configuration step. pyramids-core resolves the backend at runtime and routes its lazy operations to it:

from pyramids.netcdf import NetCDF

cube = NetCDF.read_file("era5.nc")
lazy = cube.chunk({"rows": 256, "cols": 256})  # → this package's build_lazy_cube

Resolution happens two ways, both landing on the same singleton:

Path Mechanism Preferred the pyramids.compute_backend entry point → pyramids_lazy.backend:backend Fallback an optional import of pyramids_lazy, whose get_compute_backend() returns the backend

The fallback exists so an editable checkout on PYTHONPATH, with no installed distribution metadata, still works. With neither available, core's lazy operations raise a branded OptionalPackageDoesNotExist telling the user to install the lazy stack.

docs.title: The layer boundary
docs.text:
The split is the point of the package, so it is worth stating precisely.

Concern Lives in Dataset, NetCDF, DatasetCollection, FeatureCollection and every eager operation pyramids-core The ComputeBackend Protocol, its resolver, caching and collision rules pyramids.base._compute_backend The stable re-export boundary the backend imports core through pyramids.lazy_support Lazy dask-array reads, lazy cubes, Zarr I/O, kerchunk, lazy vector reads pyramids_lazy

Core publishes the contract; this package implements it. The coupling is one-directional — pyramids-lazy depends on pyramids-core, never the reverse — so core's release cadence stays independent of the dask/zarr stack.

Two further constraints are worth knowing before changing anything here:

  • Core is reached only through pyramids.lazy_support. That facade re-exports — never reimplements — the exact core primitives the lazy modules need, and is versioned by LAZY_SUPPORT_API_VERSION. Reaching into a core internal directly couples this package to core's private layout.
  • GDAL is not a dependency. The published wheel inherits the GDAL that pyramids-core vendors; declaring a second libgdal would risk an ABI mismatch rather than a version conflict.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
0.1.0, on PyPI. The v2 backend contract covers the raster (Dataset), raster-cube (NetCDF) and vector (FeatureCollection) lazy operations.

MeshDataset's own lazy surface — open_mfdataset / to_dask_dataframe / to_zarr / from_zarr on a mesh — is not part of the v2 contract. That is narrower than "mesh does not use this backend": mesh's xarray interop (pyramids/netcdf/ugrid/interop_xarray.py) does call read_array_lazy through it, so a mesh lazy read already depends on this package being installed.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This page covers installation of pyramids-lazy and its dependencies.

Item Value Distribution name pyramids-lazy Python import name pyramids_lazy Current version 0.1.0 Supported Python declared >=3.11,<4; 3.11 – 3.14 are the versions CI tests License GPL v3 
pip install pyramids-lazy           # core + the full lazy stack
pip install pyramids-lazy[parquet]  # + the OGR-Parquet vector-lazy subset

Nothing further is needed. Once installed, pyramids-core discovers the backend through its entry point and routes every lazy operation to it — there is no import to add and no setting to flip.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
• pyramids-core >= 0.79.0 (provides the pyramids import, the ComputeBackend contract and the pyramids.lazy_support facade)
  • dask >= 2024.1.0 and distributed >= 2024.1.0
  • zarr >= 3
  • fsspec >= 2024.1.0 and s3fs >= 2024.1.0
  • kerchunk >= 0.2.10 and h5py >= 3.8.0, for the NetCDF/HDF5 lazy (Zarr-reference) path

GDAL is deliberately absent from that list. It is not a dependency of this package: the pyramids-core wheel vendors its own osgeo bindings, and import pyramids is what puts them on sys.path. Nothing here installs or pins a separate GDAL — a second, ABI-mismatched libgdal on the path is a crash, not a version conflict.

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
Extra Purpose Pulls parquet the OGR-Parquet vector-lazy subset pyarrow, dask-geopandas

The parquet extra is what LazyFeatureCollection needs: its module hard-imports dask_geopandas, so the class is resolved lazily through a module-level __getattr__ and a minimal install never evaluates that file. LazyNetCDF needs only dask and imports eagerly.

docs.title: Development dependency groups
docs.text: dev and docs are PEP 735 dependency groups, not extras — they are local tooling and are deliberately not published in the package metadata.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
The repository is a pixi workspace. Its only conda dependency is the interpreter (python >=3.11,<3.15, with one pinned feature per supported version so CI can run a per-version matrix); everything else — including pyramids-core, dask, zarr, kerchunk, h5py and the parquet extra — is resolved from PyPI through [tool.pixi.pypi-dependencies] and the PEP 735 groups. GDAL therefore arrives with the pyramids-core wheel, which vendors it, exactly as in a plain pip install.

git clone https://github.com/serapeum-org/pyramids-lazy.git
cd pyramids-lazy
pixi run -e dev test

Environments are per-Python: base (3.11 without the parquet extra), py311 … py314 (the full stack on each supported interpreter), dev (a newest-float convenience env) and docs.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: pyramids-lazy is tested with pytest, driven through pixi, and selected with markers. There are two kinds of suite plus a separate performance-benchmark suite, and everything the CI runs is reproducible locally with a pixi task.

docs.title: Test layout
docs.text:
• tests/test_*.py (top level) — the plugin's own seam / unit tests: test_backend_contract.py (the ComputeBackend Protocol, the singleton, api_version), test_seam_version.py (the import-time core-contract check), test_optional_parquet_guard.py (the [parquet] guard), plus focused test_zarr.py / test_collection_zarr.py / test_netcdf_lazy.py / test_vector_read.py.
  • tests/dataset/, tests/netcdf/lazy/, tests/feature/lazy/ — the comprehensive suites relocated verbatim from pyramids-core, keeping core's directory layout so they stay diffable against it.
  • benchmarks/ — the performance benchmarks, deliberately outside testpaths = ["tests"], so the normal test tasks never collect them (see Benchmarks).

docs.title: Environments
docs.text:
The repo carries its own self-contained pixi environments (GDAL and the native dask/zarr/HDF5 stack come from conda-forge; src/ is installed editable). Seven are defined:

Environment What it is dev everything, including the [parquet] vector extra — the day-to-day env base the no-[parquet] shape on Python 3.11 (the combo that surfaced the backend-discovery bug) py311–py314 full-stack, one per supported Python — the CI test matrix docs the MkDocs stack

Always drive them through pixi run (never a hardcoded interpreter path — a bare interpreter fails on GDAL).

docs.title: Running tests locally
docs.text:
$M = "<repo>/pyproject.toml"

# whole suite (pytest -vvv)
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev test
# with coverage, exactly as CI runs it: `main` (-m "not live", writes coverage.xml) or `test-all` (everything)
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev main

# one file / class / test
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev python -m pytest tests/netcdf/lazy/test_lazy_cube.py -q
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev python -m pytest tests/netcdf/lazy/test_lazy_cube.py::TestChunksProperty -q

# by marker
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev python -m pytest tests -q -m "not live"

# quality gates (also enforced in CI)
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev typecheck     # mypy
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev lint          # ruff check + ruff format --check
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev pydocstyle    # google convention, D403 relaxed
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev precommit     # all pre-commit hooks

docs.title: Markers
docs.text:
Test categories are selected by marker + -m only — never by an environment variable. The markers are declared in pyproject.toml:

Marker Needs core nothing beyond the base install (auto-applied when no extras marker is present) lazy the dask/zarr lazy stack netcdf_lazy kerchunk + h5py parquet the [parquet] extra (pyarrow) parquet_lazy dask-geopandas live a real external network service

Select or skip with -m, e.g. -m "not live" (the default in CI), -m parquet_lazy. live tests are skipped unless live appears as a whole token in -m.

docs.title: What runs in CI
docs.text:
Workflow What it does tests.yml matrix os × [py311, py312, py313, py314] + a no-[parquet] base leg; runs the main task (coverage → Codecov), the nbval notebooks step, and asserts the committed lock with --locked lint.yml a pre-commit job (ruff/pydocstyle/file hooks), a static job (mypy + src doctests), and a gitleaks secret scan pip-audit.yml advisory audit of the py311 lock, on PR + a weekly schedule pure-wheel-test.yml builds the wheel, installs it --only-binary=:all:, imports it and runs the suite across the matrix

Line + branch coverage is uploaded to Codecov — browse it at https://app.codecov.io/gh/serapeum-org/pyramids-lazy.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text:
The benchmarks/ suite is a set of pytest-benchmark micro-benchmarks for the compute backend's hot paths. They answer "did this change make operation X slower?" — regression detection, not profiling. Because they are outside testpaths, the normal test tasks never collect them; they run only via the benchmark task and the nightly workflow.

What is covered (the backend's lazy paths, plus an eager-core baseline):

  • benchmarks/test_bench_zarr.py — write_dataset_to_zarr (plain + overview levels) and read_dataset_from_zarr, the only fully-parallel raster Zarr write/read path (called on the backend singleton directly).
  • benchmarks/test_bench_netcdf.py — NetCDF.read_array eager vs lazy (read_array_lazy / build_lazy_array, build-only and build+compute) and NetCDF.chunk (build_lazy_cube).

Running them:

pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev benchmark                        # the whole suite, with a stats table
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev pytest benchmarks -k zarr        # one group
# save a baseline on a branch you trust, then compare a change against it
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev pytest benchmarks --benchmark-autosave
pixi run --manifest-path "$M" -e dev pytest benchmarks --benchmark-compare --benchmark-compare-fail=median:50%

Saved runs live under .benchmarks/ (git-ignored). See benchmarks/README.md for the methodology notes.

docs.title: Where to check the benchmark results
docs.text:
The benchmarks run on a nightly schedule (04:00 UTC) and on manual dispatch — never on a pull request, and only once the workflow is on the default branch. They are not a merge gate: shared GitHub runners are too noisy to compare absolute milliseconds commit-to-commit.

  • Workflow runs: https://github.com/serapeum-org/pyramids-lazy/actions/workflows/benchmarks.yml
  • Results: each run uploads a benchmark-results-<run_id> artifact (90-day retention) containing benchmark-results.json (the full --benchmark-json) and the .benchmarks/ autosave. Download it from the run's Artifacts section, or with the CLI:
gh run list --workflow benchmarks.yml
gh run download <run-id>
  • Trend chart: https://serapeum-org.github.io/pyramids-lazy/bench/ — each nightly run feeds github-action-benchmark, which appends the run to a history under bench/ on the gh-pages branch and publishes the interactive chart there. bench/ is its own subdir, so it coexists with the mike-versioned MkDocs site without either clobbering the other.
  • Regression alerts: when a benchmark regresses by ≥ 1.5× (the 150% alert threshold, loose on purpose because shared runners are noisy), the action posts a commit comment that @-mentions the maintainer. It never fails the nightly run. Alerts begin from the second run on gh-pages (the first seeds the baseline).
  • Comparing runs locally: compare two runs' JSON directly:
pytest-benchmark compare old.json new.json

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The API surface of pyramids_lazy, generated from the docstrings by mkdocstrings.

What this package publishes is one backend object, not an API you call directly. It is registered with pyramids-core through the pyramids.compute_backend entry-point group, so installing the package is the whole integration: pyramids then dispatches every lazy operation to it.

from pyramids.netcdf import NetCDF

cube = NetCDF.read_file("era5.nc")
arr = cube.read_array(variable="pr", chunks="auto")  # → this package's read_array_lazy

So the backend contract below is the surface that matters. Each method forwards to one implementation module, and each module has its own page.

docs.title: The contract itself
docs.text:
pyramids.base._compute_backend.ComputeBackend is the authoritative Protocol — the method signatures here mirror it one-for-one, and it is the file to read before changing one. The backend declares an api_version that core checks on resolution; adding a Protocol method is additive and does not bump it, while removing a name or changing semantics does.

Two public view classes are re-exported from the package root, because core forwards its own public pyramids.netcdf.LazyNetCDF and pyramids.feature.LazyFeatureCollection names — and their isinstance checks — to them:

  • LazyNetCDF — a wrapper holding one dask array per gridded variable
  • LazyFeatureCollection — a dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame subclass

docs.title: pyramids_lazy
docs.text:
pyramids-lazy: the lazy / dask compute backend for pyramids.

This package implements the ComputeBackend contract published by pyramids-core and registers it under the pyramids.compute_backend entry-point group. Installing pyramids-lazy alongside pyramids-core turns on every lazy/dask operation (raster, raster-cube and vector) without the dask/zarr stack ever being pulled into a bare pyramids-core install.

Discovery works two ways, both resolving to the same singleton :data:backend:

  • the pyramids.compute_backend entry point (pyramids_lazy.backend:backend), the path core prefers; and
  • :func:get_compute_backend, the first-party fallback core calls by name when no entry point is registered (e.g. an editable checkout on PYTHONPATH with no installed metadata).

The lazy view classes are also public here so core can forward its public pyramids.netcdf.LazyNetCDF / pyramids.feature.LazyFeatureCollection names (and their isinstance checks) to them. :class:LazyNetCDF imports eagerly (it needs only dask at call time); LazyFeatureCollection is resolved lazily via module __getattr__ because its module hard-imports dask_geopandas (the [parquet] extra).

docs.title: get_compute_backend()
docs.text:
Return the singleton compute backend (core's first-party fallback entry point).

pyramids.base._compute_backend.require_compute_backend calls this by name when no backend is registered on the pyramids.compute_backend entry-point group, so the plugin is usable from a bare checkout on PYTHONPATH as well as from an installed distribution.

docs.title: Backend contract
docs.text:
The object pyramids-core resolves and dispatches to. One instance exposing one method per lazy operation, two class accessors (lazy_netcdf_type and lazy_feature_collection_type, which hand core the classes it forwards its own public names to) and an api_version core checks before using it.

Entry-point group pyramids.compute_backend Entry point lazy = pyramids_lazy.backend:backend Fallback pyramids_lazy.get_compute_backend() Contract version API_VERSION = 2 Authoritative Protocol pyramids.base._compute_backend.ComputeBackend

Every method is a thin forwarder that imports its implementation module inside the method body, so an operation's own module (_zarr, _kerchunk_facade, _vector_read, …) is loaded only when that operation is first used.

That is a statement about the per-operation modules, not about dask. With the [parquet] extra installed, importing pyramids_lazy pulls in dask (core, array and dataframe) along with dask_geopandas, pyarrow, pandas, geopandas and scipy — though not distributed, zarr or xarray, which stay out until an operation needs them. None of this is caused by anything in this package. Nothing in pyramids_lazy, and nothing in pyramids-core, imports dask at module scope. The chain is:

  1. pyramids_lazy/__init__.py re-exports LazyNetCDF eagerly, which imports pyramids.lazy_support;
  2. that facade imports core subpackages, reaching pyramids.feature.__init__;
  3. which probes for dask_geopandas at module scope — a try/except OptionalPackageDoesNotExist that sets the _HAS_DASK_GEOPANDAS flag core uses for dispatch;
  4. and dask_geopandas imports dask.

So the cost appears only when the optional dependency is present. Blocking dask_geopandas to simulate a bare install, the probe fails, the flag goes False and no dask is imported:

Imported Modules dask present pyramids 306 no pyramids.feature, with dask_geopandas blocked 855 no pyramids.feature 1397 yes pyramids.dataset 1690 yes pyramids_lazy 1868 yes

Measured:

Measured in two separate interpreters:

$ python -c "import sys, pyramids;      print(len(sys.modules), 'dask' in sys.modules)"
306 False
$ python -c "import sys, pyramids_lazy; print(len(sys.modules), 'dask' in sys.modules)"
1868 True

What the deferred imports buy is therefore narrower than "no dask on import": zarr stays out until a Zarr operation runs, and the per-operation modules stay unloaded until used.

docs.title: Why a singleton
docs.text:
The Protocol describes a single object rather than a class discovered per source, mirroring core's plot-backend seam rather than its raster/vector driver seam. Both discovery paths resolve to the same module-level backend instance.

That is a statement about which object they return, not about patching. Core caches the backend it resolved, so a test that replaces pyramids_lazy.backend after resolution will not be seen by core until the cache is cleared (clear_compute_backend_cache).

docs.title: pyramids_lazy.backend.LazyComputeBackend
docs.text:
Concrete pyramids.compute_backend backend for the dask/zarr lazy layer.

See pyramids.base._compute_backend.ComputeBackend for the authoritative method contract and signatures; every Protocol method is implemented here one-for-one. classify_zarr_store is an additional, duck-typed extension core reaches via getattr -- deliberately not a Protocol member, so a backend predating it is not rejected by core's structural check.

Source code in src/pyramids_lazy/backend.py 
class LazyComputeBackend:
    """Concrete ``pyramids.compute_backend`` backend for the dask/zarr lazy layer.

    See ``pyramids.base._compute_backend.ComputeBackend`` for the authoritative method contract and
    signatures; every Protocol method is implemented here one-for-one. ``classify_zarr_store`` is an
    additional, duck-typed extension core reaches via ``getattr`` -- deliberately not a Protocol
    member, so a backend predating it is not rejected by core's structural check.
    """

    api_version: int = API_VERSION

    def lazy_netcdf_type(self) -> type:
        """Return the class :meth:`build_lazy_cube` produces.

        Core forwards its public ``pyramids.netcdf.LazyNetCDF`` name (and the ``isinstance`` checks
        that go with it) to this, instead of importing ``pyramids_lazy`` itself, so the entry-point
        seam stays honest about which backend is installed.
        """
        from pyramids_lazy._lazy_cube import LazyNetCDF

        return LazyNetCDF

    def lazy_feature_collection_type(self) -> type:
        """Return the class the lazy vector reads produce.

        Backs core's public ``pyramids.feature.LazyFeatureCollection`` and ``is_lazy_fc``.

        A method, NOT a property: ``runtime_checkable`` isinstance evaluates data members with
        ``getattr``, so as a property this body ran whenever core merely type-checked the backend.
        Importing the module needs ``dask-geopandas`` (the ``[parquet]`` extra), so that made the
        whole backend fail its structural check in every env without that extra -- and core, which
        treats a failing backend as one to skip, then fell back to eager execution for raster and
        cube work that never needed vectors at all. As a method the import is deferred to the call,
        where the branded hint is the right answer.
        """
        from pyramids_lazy._lazy_collection import LazyFeatureCollection

        return LazyFeatureCollection

    def read_array_lazy(
        self, dataset: Any, *, chunks: Any, lock: Any = None, **kwargs: Any
    ) -> Any:
        """Lazy dask-backed read of a raster/variable (``Dataset``/``NetCDF`` ``read_array``).

        ``dataset`` is accepted for the Protocol; the object-specific prep (path, variable name,
        spatial-dim orientation, manager hook, cloud env) is done by core and forwarded in
        ``kwargs`` to :func:`build_lazy_array`.
        """
        from pyramids_lazy._lazy import build_lazy_array

        return build_lazy_array(chunks=chunks, lock=lock, **kwargs)

    def build_lazy_cube(self, netcdf: Any, chunks: Any) -> Any:
        """Build the lazy cube view for ``NetCDF.chunk`` (returns a ``LazyNetCDF``)."""
        from pyramids_lazy._lazy_cube import build_lazy_cube

        return build_lazy_cube(netcdf, chunks)

    def to_dask_dataframe(
        self, netcdf: Any, *, variables: Any, dropna: bool, chunks: Any
    ) -> Any:
        """Back ``NetCDF.to_dask_dataframe``."""
        from pyramids_lazy._to_dask_dataframe import to_dask_dataframe

        return to_dask_dataframe(
            netcdf, variables=variables, dropna=dropna, chunks=chunks
        )

    def to_kerchunk(self, source: Any, output_path: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> dict:
        """Back ``NetCDF.to_kerchunk`` (single-file kerchunk manifest)."""
        from pyramids_lazy._kerchunk_facade import to_kerchunk

        return to_kerchunk(source, output_path, **kwargs)

    def combine_kerchunk(self, paths: Any, output_path: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> dict:
        """Back ``NetCDF.combine_kerchunk`` / ``DatasetCollection.to_kerchunk``."""
        from pyramids_lazy._kerchunk_facade import combine_kerchunk

        return combine_kerchunk(paths, output_path, **kwargs)

    def open_mfdataset(self, paths: Any, variable: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Back ``NetCDF.open_mfdataset`` (dask-stacked multi-file read)."""
        from pyramids_lazy._mfdataset import open_mfdataset

        return open_mfdataset(paths, variable, **kwargs)

    def write_dataset_to_zarr(self, dataset: Any, store: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Back ``Dataset.to_zarr``."""
        from pyramids_lazy._zarr import write_dataset_to_zarr

        return write_dataset_to_zarr(dataset, store, **kwargs)

    def read_dataset_from_zarr(self, store: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Back ``Dataset.from_zarr`` (returns a ``Dataset``)."""
        from pyramids_lazy._zarr import read_dataset_from_zarr

        return read_dataset_from_zarr(store, **kwargs)

    def classify_zarr_store(
        self, store: Any, storage_options: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> str:
        """Back core's ``Dataset.read_file`` Zarr routing: classify a ``.zarr`` store.

        Returns ``"single"`` / ``"cube"`` / ``"other"``. Core applies the cheap suffix gate itself
        and asks the backend to look inside a ``.zarr``; opening the store needs the optional
        ``zarr`` package, which lives here, so the classification does too. An unreadable or foreign
        store is reported as ``"other"`` (never raises) so core falls back to GDAL.
        """
        from pyramids_lazy._zarr import classify_zarr_store

        return classify_zarr_store(store, storage_options)

    def write_collection_to_zarr(
        self, collection: Any, store: Any, **kwargs: Any
    ) -> Any:
        """Back ``DatasetCollection.to_zarr``."""
        from pyramids_lazy._collection_zarr import write_collection_to_zarr

        return write_collection_to_zarr(collection, store, **kwargs)

    def read_collection_from_zarr(
        self, collection_cls: Any, store: Any, **kwargs: Any
    ) -> Any:
        """Back ``DatasetCollection.from_zarr`` (returns a ``DatasetCollection``)."""
        from pyramids_lazy._collection_zarr import read_collection_from_zarr

        return read_collection_from_zarr(collection_cls, store, **kwargs)

    def read_vector_lazy(self, source: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Back ``FeatureCollection.read_file(backend="dask")``."""
        from pyramids_lazy._vector_read import read_file_dask

        return read_file_dask(source, **kwargs)

    def read_vector_parquet_lazy(self, source: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Back ``FeatureCollection.read_parquet(backend="dask")``."""
        from pyramids_lazy._vector_read import read_parquet_dask

        return read_parquet_dask(source, **kwargs)

    """Import and return ``dask_geopandas``, or raise a branded ``ImportError``.

    Called at module scope by every module that needs ``dask_geopandas``, so the branded hint is
    raised on a cold import too — not only by the call-time guards, which a warm ``sys.modules``
    is all that lets them be reached.

    Returns:
        The imported ``dask_geopandas`` module.

    Raises:
        LazyExtraNotInstalled: When ``dask_geopandas`` is not installed, naming
            ``pyramids-lazy[parquet]``. A ``ModuleNotFoundError`` subclass, so optional-import
            guards and :func:`pytest.importorskip` keep treating it as "absent" rather than
            "broken".

    Examples:
        - The result is the `dask_geopandas` module itself, so its API is reached straight off it:
            ```python
            >>> from pyramids_lazy._optional import import_dask_geopandas
            >>> module = import_dask_geopandas()  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> module.__name__  # doctest: +SKIP
            'dask_geopandas'
            >>> module.GeoDataFrame.__name__  # doctest: +SKIP
            'GeoDataFrame'

            ```
        - Every call hands back the single module object `sys.modules` already holds, so calling it
          at module scope and again inside a call-time guard costs one import:

            ```python
            >>> import_dask_geopandas() is import_dask_geopandas()  # doctest: +SKIP
            True

            ```

docs.title: Region append
docs.text:
A collection can be extended along an existing axis without rewriting the store: the new data is written into a region of the existing arrays, and the collection metadata (_meta, _files) is re-finalised afterwards so a later read reconstructs the full cube. The region is translated to per-axis slices, and an unknown dimension name is refused with a ValueError.

Chunk-grid alignment is not validated. A region that straddles a chunk boundary is written as given, so it is the caller's job to append on the chunk grid.

As with the single-Dataset path, the pyramids geobox is persisted as GeoZarr attributes so standard readers can reconstruct it.

def write_collection_to_zarr(
    collection: Any,
    store: str | Path | Any,
    *,
    compute: bool = True,
    mode: str = "w",
    storage_options: dict | None = None,
    compressor: Any = "auto",
    append_dim: str | None = None,
    region: dict | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Serialise the 4-D ``(T, B, R, C)`` cube of ``collection`` to a Zarr store.

    Each dask chunk in ``collection.data`` lands in an independent Zarr chunk file. Geobox metadata
    is written as attributes on the root group + the ``data`` array. See
    :meth:`DatasetCollection.to_zarr` for the full argument contract.
    """
    files = collection._require_files("to_zarr")
    import_zarr(
        lazy_hint("DatasetCollection.to_zarr requires the 'zarr' dependency.", "zarr")
    )
    if mode == "a" and append_dim is None and region is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "mode='a' requires append_dim='time' or region=... (append_dim / "
            "region semantics); use mode='w' to (over)write the whole cube."
        )
    data = collection.data
    resolved_store = _resolve_store(store, storage_options)
    codec_kwargs = normalize_compressors(compressor)

    if append_dim is not None:
        return _append_to_zarr(collection, resolved_store, data, append_dim, compute)
    if region is not None:
        import zarr

        existing = zarr.open_group(resolved_store, mode="a")["data"]
        return data.to_zarr(
            existing,
            region=_region_to_slices(region, data.ndim),
            overwrite=False,
            compute=compute,
        )

    write_result = data.to_zarr(
        resolved_store,
        component="data",
        overwrite=(mode == "w"),
        compute=compute,
        **codec_kwargs,
    )
    if compute:
        _finalize_collection_metadata(resolved_store, collection._meta, files)
        result: Any = None
    else:
        import dask

        result = dask.delayed(_finalize_after_write)(
            write_result,
            resolved_store,
            collection._meta,
            files,
        )
    return result

Inverse of :func:write_collection_to_zarr. The 4-D (time, band, y, x) data array is read lazily straight from the store, and the geobox is recovered from the GeoZarr spatial_ref mapping. collection_cls is the DatasetCollection class to construct.

def read_collection_from_zarr(
    collection_cls: Any,
    store: str | Path | Any,
    *,
    storage_options: dict | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Open a pyramids-written cube Zarr store into a lazy ``DatasetCollection``.

    Inverse of :func:`write_collection_to_zarr`. The 4-D ``(time, band, y, x)`` ``data`` array is
    read lazily straight from the store, and the geobox is recovered from the GeoZarr ``spatial_ref``
    mapping. ``collection_cls`` is the ``DatasetCollection`` class to construct.
    """
    import_zarr(
        lazy_hint(
            "DatasetCollection.from_zarr requires the 'zarr' dependency.",
            "zarr",
        )
    )
    import zarr

    resolved = _resolve_store(store, storage_options)
    root = zarr.open_group(resolved, mode="r")
    data_arr = root["data"]
    if not isinstance(data_arr, zarr.Array):
        raise TypeError(
            f"expected the 'data' node in {resolved!r} to be a zarr Array, "
            f"got a Group -- the store is not a pyramids cube"
        )
    data_attrs = dict(data_arr.attrs)
    geobox = read_geobox(root, data_name="data")
    time_length, bands, rows, cols = (int(v) for v in data_arr.shape)
    time_length = int(
        cast("int | float | str", root.attrs.get("time_length", time_length))
    )

    nodata_list = cast("list | None", data_attrs.get("nodata"))
    if nodata_list and any(v is not None for v in nodata_list):
        no_data_value: Any = list(nodata_list)
    else:
        no_data_value = None
    dtype = np.dtype(cast(str, data_attrs.get("dtype", "float32")))
    template_arr = np.zeros((bands, rows, cols), dtype=dtype)
    geo_6 = cast(
        "tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float]",
        tuple(float(v) for v in geobox["geotransform"]),
    )
    template = Dataset.from_array(
        template_arr if bands > 1 else template_arr[0],
        no_data_value=no_data_value,
        geo_ref=GeoReference(geo=geo_6, epsg=geobox_crs(geobox)),
    )
    if geobox["crs_wkt"]:
        template.crs = geobox["crs_wkt"]
    template.bands.apply_names(
        cast("list | None", data_attrs.get("band_names")),
        source="cube Zarr store",
    )
    meta = RasterMeta.from_dataset(template)
    return collection_cls(template, time_length, meta=meta, zarr_store=resolved)

Hand nc's cube to dask in tidy form — the lazy sibling of to_dataframe.

Returns a :class:dask.dataframe.DataFrame with the dimension coordinates as plain columns beside the value columns on a flat index. Values are read lazily through NetCDF.read_array.

def to_dask_dataframe(
    nc: Any, *, variables: Any = None, dropna: bool = False, chunks: Any = "auto"
) -> Any:
    """Hand ``nc``'s cube to dask in tidy form — the lazy sibling of ``to_dataframe``.

    Returns a :class:`dask.dataframe.DataFrame` with the dimension coordinates as plain columns
    beside the value columns on a flat index. Values are read lazily through ``NetCDF.read_array``.
    """
    import_dask(_DASK_MISSING)
    require_optional(
        "dask.dataframe",
        "to_dask_dataframe() needs dask.dataframe, which requires pyarrow — install the "
        "`parquet` extra (e.g. `pip install pyramids-lazy[parquet]`).",
    )
    import dask.array as da
    import dask.dataframe as dd

    names = _frame_variables(nc, variables)
    first = nc._require_raster_variable(names[0]) if _is_container(nc) else nc
    in_memory = _is_in_memory(nc)
    value_arrays = _lazy_value_columns(nc, names, first, in_memory, chunks, da)
    ref_chunks = next(iter(value_arrays.values())).chunks
    columns = _lazy_dimension_columns(first, ref_chunks, da)
    for name, array in value_arrays.items():
        columns[name] = array.rechunk(ref_chunks)
    frame = dd.concat(
        [dd.from_dask_array(col, columns=[label]) for label, col in columns.items()],
        axis=1,
    )
    return frame.dropna(subset=list(names), how="all") if dropna else frame

docs.title: Two builders, and why
docs.text:
The facade dispatches between kerchunk's own translators and a native builder in this package.

The native builder exists because of a deadlock: kerchunk.hdf drives zarr's synchronous v2 API, which under zarr v3 submits work to a process-global event loop and hangs intermittently. The builder walks the HDF5 container with h5py and emits zarr-v2 metadata plus byte-range chunk references directly, never instantiating a live zarr group. Its output is the ordinary kerchunk reference document, so the consumer side is unchanged.

Its scope is the feature surface GDAL's netCDF driver writes: fixed-width numeric and fixed-length string dtypes, deflate/shuffle filters, and dimension scales. An unsupported HDF5 feature raises a clear ValueError rather than producing a subtly wrong manifest.

def to_kerchunk(
    src_path: str | Path,
    output_path: str | Path,
    *,
    inline_threshold: int = 500,
    vlen_encode: str = "embed",
    backend: str = "native",
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Emit a single-file kerchunk reference manifest.

    Args:
        src_path: Path or URL of the source NetCDF / HDF5 file.
        output_path: Path where the JSON manifest is written.
        inline_threshold: Chunks smaller than this many bytes are
            embedded directly in the manifest rather than referenced
            by offset.
        vlen_encode: One of `"embed" | "null" | "leave" | "encode"`.
            Controls how VLEN (variable-length) strings are handled.
            Default `"embed"` inlines string values; other modes
            trade compatibility vs fidelity — see the kerchunk docs.
        backend: `"native"` (default) builds the manifest directly with
            h5py — no live zarr group, so it cannot hit the zarr-v3
            `sync()` deadlock (#530). `"legacy"` forces the
            `kerchunk.hdf.SingleHdf5ToZarr` translator. The native
            backend falls back to the legacy translator for files using
            HDF5 features it does not support (e.g. vlen/compound dtypes).
            `"kerchunk"` is a deprecated alias for `"legacy"`.

    Returns:
        The manifest dict that was written — useful for inspection
        or further programmatic use.

    Raises:
        ImportError: When the chosen backend's dependency is missing
            (h5py for `"native"`, kerchunk for `"legacy"`).
        ValueError: When `backend` is not `"native"` or `"legacy"`.

    Examples:
        - Emit a manifest for one NetCDF file (requires kerchunk, a
          pyramids-lazy dependency):
            ```python
            >>> from pathlib import Path  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> from pyramids_lazy._kerchunk_facade import to_kerchunk  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> manifest = to_kerchunk(
            ...     "noah_20240101.nc", "noah_20240101.kerchunk.json",
            ... )  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> "refs" in manifest or "version" in manifest  # doctest: +SKIP
            True

            ```
    """
    backend = _normalize_backend(backend)
    src_str = str(src_path)

    def _legacy() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return _kerchunk_translate_single(
            src_str, inline_threshold=inline_threshold, vlen_encode=vlen_encode
        )

    if backend == "legacy":
        refs = _legacy()
    else:
        refs = _native_or_fallback(
            lambda: build_single_manifest(
                src_str, inline_threshold=inline_threshold, vlen_encode=vlen_encode
            ),
            _legacy,
            local_inputs_exist=os.path.exists(src_str),
            subject=f"native kerchunk builder could not handle {src_str!r}",
        )
    Path(output_path).write_text(json.dumps(refs))
    return refs

>>> srcs = sorted(Path("/data/noah").glob("noah_*.nc"))  # doctest: +SKIP

def combine_kerchunk(
    src_paths: Sequence[str | Path],
    output_path: str | Path,
    *,
    concat_dims: Sequence[str] = ("time",),
    identical_dims: Sequence[str] = ("lat", "lon"),
    inline_threshold: int = 500,
    backend: str = "native",
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Emit a combined kerchunk manifest spanning many source files.

    The default `"native"` backend scans each file with :func:`build_single_manifest`
    (h5py, no live zarr group) and concatenates the per-file manifests along the
    single `concat_dims` entry — every variable carrying that dimension is stacked,
    the rest are carried from the first file. This avoids the zarr-v3 `sync()`
    deadlock (#530). `"legacy"` forces the
    `SingleHdf5ToZarr` + `MultiZarrToZarr` path; the native backend also falls back
    to it for inputs it cannot handle (e.g. multiple concat dims, unsupported HDF5
    features). `"kerchunk"` is a deprecated alias for `"legacy"`.

    Args:
        src_paths: Sequence of source NetCDF / HDF5 paths or URLs, in
            concatenation order.
        output_path: Path where the combined JSON manifest is written.
        concat_dims: Dimension name(s) along which to concatenate. The native
            backend supports exactly one; more than one falls back to kerchunk.
            Default `("time",)`.
        identical_dims: Dimension name(s) expected to be identical across files
            (e.g. shared `lat`/`lon`). Used by the kerchunk backend; the native
            backend treats every non-concat variable as identical implicitly.
            Default `("lat", "lon")`.
        inline_threshold: Same semantics as :func:`to_kerchunk`.
        backend: `"native"` (default) or `"legacy"` (`"kerchunk"` is a deprecated alias).

    Returns:
        The combined manifest dict that was written.

    Raises:
        ImportError: When the chosen backend's dependency is missing.
        ValueError: When `backend` is not `"native"` or `"legacy"`.

    Examples:
        - Combine a year's worth of daily NetCDFs into one manifest:
            ```python
            >>> from pathlib import Path  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> from pyramids_lazy._kerchunk_facade import combine_kerchunk  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> srcs = sorted(Path("/data/noah").glob("noah_*.nc"))  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> manifest = combine_kerchunk(
            ...     srcs, "noah_combined.json",
            ...     concat_dims=("time",),
            ... )  # doctest: +SKIP
            >>> "refs" in manifest or "version" in manifest  # doctest: +SKIP
            True

            ```
    """
    backend = _normalize_backend(backend)

    def _legacy() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return _kerchunk_combine(
            src_paths,
            concat_dims=concat_dims,
            identical_dims=identical_dims,
            inline_threshold=inline_threshold,
        )

    def _native() -> dict[str, Any]:
        if len(concat_dims) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                "native combine supports exactly one concat dimension; got "
                f"{tuple(concat_dims)}"
            )
        per_file = [
            build_single_manifest(str(path), inline_threshold=inline_threshold)
            for path in src_paths
        ]
        return combine_manifests(per_file, concat_dim=concat_dims[0])

    if backend == "legacy":
        combined = _legacy()
    else:
        combined = _native_or_fallback(
            _native,
            _legacy,
            local_inputs_exist=all(os.path.exists(str(path)) for path in src_paths),
            subject="native kerchunk combine could not handle these inputs",
        )
    Path(output_path).write_text(json.dumps(combined))
    return combined

def build_single_manifest(
    src_path: str | Path,
    *,
    src_url: str | None = None,
    inline_threshold: int = 500,
    vlen_encode: str = "embed",
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a kerchunk v1 reference manifest for one NetCDF4 / HDF5 file.

    Args:
        src_path: Local path used to read chunk byte ranges and HDF5 metadata.
        src_url: URL written into byte-range references. Defaults to
            ``str(src_path)`` so the manifest points back at the source as
            named (matching kerchunk's behaviour for local paths).
        inline_threshold: Chunks smaller than this many bytes are embedded
            directly (base64) rather than referenced by offset.
        vlen_encode: VLEN string handling mode (reserved; object dtypes are
            currently rejected with a clear error).

    Returns:
        The manifest dict ``{"version": 1, "refs": {...}}``.

    Raises:
        ImportError: When h5py is not installed.
        ValueError: When the file uses an unsupported HDF5 feature.
    """
    h5py = _require_h5py()
    src_str = str(src_path)
    src_local = src_str if os.path.exists(src_str) else None
    if src_url is not None:
        url = src_url
    elif src_local is not None:
        # Absolutise local paths so the manifest resolves regardless of the
        # consumer's working directory, and use forward slashes (as_posix) so a
        # Windows-written manifest carries a portable path rather than back-slashes
        # that some fsspec/zarr consumers mishandle.
        url = Path(src_str).resolve().as_posix()
    else:
        url = src_str

    refs: dict[str, Any] = {}
    # One binary handle for the whole walk so inlined chunks don't reopen the file
    # per chunk; None for a remote source (those are always referenced, not inlined).
    src_handle = open(src_local, "rb") if src_local is not None else None
    try:
        with h5py.File(src_str, "r") as h5file:
            refs[_ZARR_GROUP] = json.dumps({"zarr_format": 2})
            refs[_ZARR_ATTRS] = json.dumps(_clean_attrs(h5file.attrs), allow_nan=False)

            def visit(name: str, obj: Any) -> None:
                if isinstance(obj, h5py.Dataset):
                    _emit_dataset(
                        refs,
                        h5file=h5file,
                        name=name,
                        dataset=obj,
                        src_url=url,
                        src_handle=src_handle,
                        inline_threshold=inline_threshold,
                        vlen_encode=vlen_encode,
                    )
                else:
                    refs[f"{name}/{_ZARR_GROUP}"] = json.dumps({"zarr_format": 2})
                    refs[f"{name}/{_ZARR_ATTRS}"] = json.dumps(
                        _clean_attrs(obj.attrs), allow_nan=False
                    )

            h5file.visititems(visit)
    finally:
        if src_handle is not None:
            src_handle.close()

    return {"version": 1, "refs": refs}

def combine_manifests(
    per_file: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    concat_dim: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Concatenate per-file manifests along ``concat_dim`` into one manifest.

    Every variable whose ``_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS`` contains ``concat_dim`` is stacked
    along that axis (its concat-axis chunk indices are renumbered and its
    ``shape`` summed); every other variable must be identical across files and is
    carried from the first. No zarr group is created, so this cannot hit the
    zarr-v3 ``sync()`` deadlock (#530).

    Args:
        per_file: Per-file manifests, in concatenation order, as returned by
            :func:`build_single_manifest`.
        concat_dim: Dimension name to concatenate along.

    Returns:
        The combined manifest dict ``{"version": 1, "refs": {...}}``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``per_file`` is empty, files disagree on the variable
            set, a concat variable has inconsistent chunking, or a non-concat
            variable is not identical across files.
    """
    if not per_file:
        raise ValueError("combine_manifests requires at least one manifest.")
    refs_list = [_manifest_refs(m) for m in per_file]
    if len(refs_list) == 1:
        return {"version": 1, "refs": dict(refs_list[0])}

    var_sets = [set(_variable_names(refs)) for refs in refs_list]
    if any(names != var_sets[0] for names in var_sets[1:]):
        raise ValueError(
            "cannot combine manifests with differing variable sets: "
            f"{[sorted(names) for names in var_sets]}"
        )

    combined: dict[str, Any] = {}
    variables = set(_variable_names(refs_list[0]))
    for key, value in refs_list[0].items():
        is_root_meta = "/" not in key
        is_subgroup_meta = (
            key.endswith((_ZARR_GROUP, _ZARR_ATTRS))
            and key.rsplit("/", 1)[0] not in variables
        )
        # carry root metadata and sub-group metadata (not owned by a variable)
        if is_root_meta or is_subgroup_meta:
            combined[key] = value

    for name in _variable_names(refs_list[0]):
        dims = json.loads(refs_list[0][f"{name}/{_ZARR_ATTRS}"]).get(
            "_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS", []
        )
        if concat_dim in dims:
            combined.update(_concat_variable(name, refs_list, dims.index(concat_dim)))
        else:
            combined.update(_identical_variable(name, refs_list))

    return {"version": 1, "refs": combined}

docs.title: Lazy raster reads
docs.text:
Backs NetCDF.read_array(chunks=…). Returns a dask.array.Array instead of a NumPy array, without dask being imported until the call happens.

Dataset.read_array does not route here. It accepts chunks= and returns a dask.array.Array, but it is served by core's own in-core lazy raster path (pyramids.dataset.engines.IO.read_array, which never calls require_compute_backend). Every read_array_lazy call site in core lives under pyramids/netcdf/ (netcdf.py, engines/interop.py, ugrid/interop_xarray.py).

So a lazy Dataset read needs dask but not this package, whereas a lazy NetCDF read needs this package. Dataset's Zarr and kerchunk operations do come here — see Zarr (Dataset).

Backend method read_array_lazy Module pyramids_lazy._lazy Returns dask.array.Array 
from pyramids.netcdf import NetCDF

cube = NetCDF.read_file("era5.nc")
arr = cube.read_array(variable="pr", chunks={"rows": 64, "cols": 64})
arr.mean().compute()

docs.title: How the graph is built
docs.text:
The array is assembled from a low-level task graph — one pickle-safe reader task per block — rather than from dask.array.from_array. That is what makes a distributed read work: each task carries the path and window, opens the dataset through a CachingFileManager, and reads only its own window. The manager is the reason a worker handling many blocks of one file opens it once, and the reason the handle is shared process-globally rather than per task.

chunks accepts "auto", a single int, a sequence per axis, or a dict keyed by rows / cols / columns / bands (case-insensitive) or by integer axis index; normalization to an explicit per-axis tuple happens here. The keys are axis roles, not the file's dimension names, so {"time": 24} or {"x": 512} raises ValueError. Spatial-dimension orientation (flips and axis moves needed to present a plane north-up) is applied lazily, inside the graph, so it costs nothing until compute.

docs.title: Object-specific preparation stays in core
docs.text: The dataset argument exists for the Protocol's sake. Everything object-specific — resolving the path, the variable name, the spatial-dimension orientation, the manager hook and the cloud environment — is done by core and forwarded in kwargs, so this module never reaches back into a core object's internals.

def build_lazy_array(
    path: str,
    variable_name: str,
    chunks: Any,
    lock: Any = None,
    manager_id: Any = None,
    manager_hook: Any = None,
    spatial_dims: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    flips: tuple[bool, bool] | None = None,
    gdal_env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    orient: bool = True,
) -> Any:
    """Build a :class:`dask.array.Array` backed by MDArray chunk reads.

    Args:
        path: On-disk path to the NetCDF / HDF5 / Zarr file.
        variable_name: Name of the MDArray, group-qualified
            (``"flight_03/CO"``) for a variable in a sub-group.
        chunks: Raw user input — `int`, `tuple`, `dict`, or
            the string `"auto"`. See :func:`_normalize_chunks`.
        lock: Lock passed to :class:`CachingFileManager`; see
            :func:`_resolve_lock`.
        manager_id: Optional stable id so two lazy reads of the same
            variable share a cache slot. Defaults to
            `(path, variable_name)` so repeated calls for the same
            variable de-duplicate the cached handle.
        gdal_env: The dataset's captured cloud config, carried into every
            chunk task so a signed remote store authenticates the re-open each
            task performs. A no-op when empty / `None`.
        manager_hook: Optional callable invoked with the created
            `CachingFileManager` before the array is returned, so the
            owning object (e.g. the `NetCDF` container) can track it and
            release its handle from `close()` -- the second half of the
            #727 fix (release on the parent's `close()`, not only when
            the array is dropped). It should hold only a weak reference,
            so it does not defeat the drop-time finalizer.
        spatial_dims: `(x_index, y_index)` of the raster plane the eager
            `get_variable` path resolved (explicit `x_dim`/`y_dim` or CF
            detection). When given, the resolved plane is moved to the
            trailing two axes so the lazy read is oriented on the same
            plane as the eager read; `None` (the default) keeps the
            historical trailing-two-axes normalization. See
            :func:`_orient_lazy_plane` (#728).
        flips: `(needs_y_flip, needs_x_flip)` the eager path decided for
            the resolved plane. Used with `spatial_dims`; `None` falls
            back to the trailing-plane decision.
        orient: When `True` (the default) the block is normalized to the
            raster convention (row 0 = north, col 0 = west) like the eager
            `get_variable` read. Pass `False` for a raw read in the file's
            native axis order (the raw interop read path, whose coordinate
            arrays are also read raw, so the data must not be flipped relative
            to them).

    Returns:
        dask.array.Array: Lazy array that computes chunk-by-chunk
        through :func:`_read_mdarray_chunk`.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If `dask` is not installed.
        ValueError: For malformed `chunks` input or missing
            variable.
    """
    import_dask(_DASK_MISSING_MESSAGE)
    import dask.array as da
    from dask.base import tokenize

    shape, dtype, block_size, flip_y, flip_x = _mdarray_shape_and_dtype(
        path,
        variable_name,
    )
    chunk_shape = _normalize_chunks(chunks, shape, block_size, dtype)
    resolved_lock = _resolve_lock(lock)
    key_id = manager_id if manager_id is not None else (path, variable_name)
    manager = CachingFileManager(
        gdal_mdarray_open,
        path,
        "read_only",
        {},
        lock=resolved_lock,
        manager_id=key_id,
        auto_release=True,
    )
    if manager_hook is not None:
        manager_hook(manager)
    chunks_per_axis = _expand_chunks(shape, chunk_shape)
    starts_per_axis = _chunk_starts(chunks_per_axis)
    # Deterministic, content-addressed graph name (path + variable + chunking + cache key) rather
    # than `id(manager)`, so two identical lazy reads share a name and dask can dedupe them
    # (common-subexpression elimination); `id()` gave every read a fresh name and defeated CSE
    # (ARC-76).
    name = f"pyramids-netcdf-read-{variable_name}-{tokenize(path, variable_name, chunk_shape, key_id)}"
    graph: dict[tuple, Any] = {}
    grid_shape = tuple(len(sizes) for sizes in chunks_per_axis)
    for index in np.ndindex(*grid_shape):
        counts = tuple(chunks_per_axis[axis][i] for axis, i in enumerate(index))
        starts = tuple(starts_per_axis[axis][i] for axis, i in enumerate(index))
        reader = _MDArrayChunkReader(
            manager,
            variable_name,
            dtype,
            starts,
            counts,
            gdal_env,
        )
        graph[(name,) + index] = (reader,)
    lazy = da.Array(graph, name, chunks_per_axis, dtype=dtype)
    # Normalize to the raster convention the eager path produces (row 0 = north, col 0 = west) on the
    # SAME plane the eager `get_variable` resolved -- moving a non-trailing plane to the trailing two
    # axes when `spatial_dims` is threaded through (#728). A trailing plane makes this a no-op, so the
    # ordinary `(time, lev, lat, lon)` case is unchanged. Skipped for a raw read (`orient=False`),
    # which must return the file's native axis order (ARC-48 raw interop read).
    if orient:
        lazy = _orient_lazy_plane(
            lazy, da, len(shape), spatial_dims, flips, (flip_y, flip_x)
        )
    # The parked FILE_CACHE handle is released deterministically when this `manager` is
    # garbage-collected -- the `CachingFileManager` registers a `weakref.finalize` on itself in
    # `__init__`. Because the manager is kept alive by the chunk readers in the graph (not by this
    # `lazy` object), that release still fires for derived arrays -- `unpack=True`, `open_mfdataset`,
    # `plot(chunks=)` -- whose graph keeps only the readers, not this wrapper (#727).
    return lazy

def mask_no_data(arr: Any, fill: Any) -> Any:
    """Return a lazy dask masked array with `arr`'s no-data cells masked.

    The lazy counterpart of the eager `read_array(masked=True)`: cells equal to the (physical)
    `fill` — or NaN cells when `fill` is NaN — are masked, so computing the result yields a
    :class:`numpy.ma.MaskedArray`. `fill=None` (a variable with no declared no-data) yields an
    all-unmasked masked array, matching the eager path. `fill` is the sentinel **in read units**
    (physical, post-unpack); applied after `apply_unpack`, so it compares equal to the unpacked
    fill cells exactly, the same way the eager path's `_read_no_data` does.

    Args:
        arr: A :class:`dask.array.Array` of (already unpacked) values.
        fill: The physical no-data sentinel, or `None`.

    Returns:
        dask.array.Array: A dask masked array over `arr`.
    """
    import_dask(_DASK_MISSING_MESSAGE)
    import dask.array as da

    if fill is None:
        result = da.ma.masked_array(arr)
    elif np.isnan(fill):
        result = da.ma.masked_invalid(arr)
    else:
        result = da.ma.masked_equal(arr, fill)
    return result

docs.title: What it is — and is not
docs.text:
A LazyFeatureCollection is a dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame. It is not a FeatureCollection and not a geopandas.GeoDataFrame. Both it and the eager FeatureCollection satisfy core's SpatialObject protocol, so a consumer accepts either through isinstance(x, SpatialObject) rather than by checking for a concrete class.

That subclass relationship is why the whole dask-geopandas API is available directly on the object — npartitions, spatial_shuffle(), compute(), the geometry accessors — rather than being re-exposed method by method.

docs.title: Why the import is deferred
docs.text:
This module hard-imports dask_geopandas, which only the parquet extra installs. The class is therefore resolved through a module-level __getattr__ on the package root, so importing pyramids_lazy on a minimal install never evaluates this file. LazyNetCDF, which needs only dask, is imported eagerly instead.

Pickling is handled explicitly: a reconstruction hook rebuilds the subclass rather than letting dask's default reduce return a plain dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame, so a round trip through a distributed worker preserves the type.

class LazyFeatureCollection(dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame):
    """Lazy vector collection backed by a dask_geopandas graph.

    Subclasses :class:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame` — every method of that
    parent is available unchanged (`to_crs`, `clip`, `sjoin`,
    `.npartitions`, `.spatial_partitions`). Overrides: `compute` /
    `persist` return pyramids-native wrappers, `spatial_shuffle`
    re-wraps the shuffled result, `to_file` / `plot` raise with
    actionable messages, and `read_file` is a classmethod delegating
    back to the eager reader so the
    :class:`~pyramids.base.protocols.SpatialObject` protocol is satisfied.

    Construct via `FeatureCollection.read_file(..., backend='dask')` or
    `FeatureCollection.read_parquet(..., backend='dask')`. Direct
    construction is discouraged; use
    :meth:`LazyFeatureCollection.from_dask_gdf` if you must wrap a
    pre-built dask-geopandas frame.

    Note:
        On installs without the `[parquet]` extra, importing this
        class from :mod:`pyramids.feature` returns `None` (sentinel).
        Consumer code using `isinstance` must guard explicitly:
        `if LazyFeatureCollection is not None and isinstance(x, LazyFeatureCollection):...`.
    """

    def __getattribute__(self, name: str) -> Any:
        """Return a class-swapped view of every inherited method's result.

        dask-geopandas inherits from dask-expr and does not honour pandas'
        classic `_constructor` hook. Methods like `to_crs`, `clip`,
        `sjoin`, `copy`, `drop_duplicates` go through
        `map_partitions` with meta inference and produce a plain
        :class:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame`, silently dropping the
        :class:`LazyFeatureCollection` subclass. This hook wraps every
        public callable so that a :class:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame`
        result is rebranded back to the subclass before it reaches the
        caller. Private names (`_`-prefixed) are passed through
        unchanged to keep dask-expr internals — meta inference, name
        caches, partition probing — on the hot path they expect.
        """
        attr = object.__getattribute__(self, name)
        if name.startswith("_") or not callable(attr):
            return attr
        cls = type(self)

        @functools.wraps(attr)
        def wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
            result = attr(*args, **kwargs)
            if isinstance(result, dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame) and not isinstance(
                result,
                cls,
            ):
                result = cls.from_dask_gdf(result)
            elif isinstance(result, geopandas.GeoDataFrame) and not isinstance(
                result,
                geopandas.GeoSeries,
            ):
                from pyramids.feature import FeatureCollection

                # Skip the wrap when the method (e.g. an overridden `compute`) already
                # returned a FeatureCollection, avoiding a redundant double-wrap (ARC-63).
                if not isinstance(result, FeatureCollection):
                    result = FeatureCollection(result)
            return result

        return wrapper

    @classmethod
    def from_dask_gdf(cls, dask_gdf: Any) -> LazyFeatureCollection:
        """Wrap an existing :class:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame` as a LazyFC.

        This is the canonical construction path for code that already holds
        a pre-built :class:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame` (for example,
        from :func:`dask_geopandas.from_geopandas` or a third-party reader)
        and wants to use it through the pyramids type system.

        Implementation uses class-swap (`copy()` + `__class__`
        assignment) rather than a four-arg reconstruction, because
        `(dask, _name, _meta, divisions)` is private dask.dataframe API
        that shifted between dask-expr and legacy. Class-swap relies only
        on Python's object model and survives upstream churn. The
        invariant "`LazyFeatureCollection` adds no extra instance state
        beyond :class:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame`" is pinned by
        :func:`tests.feature.test_lazy_feature_collection.test_from_dask_gdf_preserves_state`.

        Args:
            dask_gdf: Pre-built `dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame` to wrap.

        Returns:
            LazyFeatureCollection: A view over `dask_gdf` whose
            `__class__` has been rebound to LazyFeatureCollection.
            The task graph, partition names, metadata, and divisions
            are unchanged — only the concrete class is swapped.

        Examples:
            - Wrap a fresh dask_geopandas frame:
                ```python
                >>> import geopandas as gpd
                >>> import dask_geopandas as dg
                >>> from shapely.geometry import Point
                >>> from pyramids.feature import LazyFeatureCollection
                >>> gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                ...     {"v": [1, 2]},
                ...     geometry=[Point(0, 0), Point(1, 1)],
                ...     crs="EPSG:4326",
                ... )
                >>> ddf = dg.from_geopandas(gdf, npartitions=1)
                >>> lfc = LazyFeatureCollection.from_dask_gdf(ddf)
                >>> lfc.npartitions
                1
                >>> lfc.epsg
                4326

                ```
        """
        result = dask_gdf.copy()
        result.__class__ = cls
        return cast("LazyFeatureCollection", result)

    # Deprecated alias kept for one release cycle. Old callsites
    # (readers inside collection.py, tests) can transition at their own
    # pace; remove the alias in a follow-up commit.
    _from_dask_gdf = from_dask_gdf

    def __reduce__(self):
        """Preserve the LazyFeatureCollection class across pickle round-trips.

        `from_dask_gdf` uses `result.__class__ = cls` to rebind the
        concrete class. The parent's default `__reduce__` reconstructs
        with the base :class:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame`, silently
        dropping the subclass on unpickle. Wrapping super's reduce tuple
        in a module-level trampoline re-applies the class swap.
        """
        return (_rebuild_lazy_fc, (super().__reduce__(),))

    @classmethod
    def read_file(
        cls,
        path: str | Path,
        *,
        npartitions: int | None = None,
        chunksize: int | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> LazyFeatureCollection:
        """Construct a LazyFC from a vector file.

        Satisfies the :class:`~pyramids.base.protocols.SpatialObject`
        protocol's `read_file` classmethod requirement. Delegates to
        :meth:`FeatureCollection.read_file` with `backend='dask'`.

        The import of :class:`FeatureCollection` is inline by
        necessity — :mod:`pyramids.feature.collection` imports this module
        from inside its dask branch, so a top-of-file import here would
        form a cycle. Per `CLAUDE.md`, circular-import breaks are an
        accepted exception to the no-inline-imports rule.

        Args:
            path: Path to a vector file GDAL/OGR can open (GeoJSON,
                Shapefile, GeoPackage, FlatGeobuf, …).
            npartitions: Target number of dask partitions. Mutually
                exclusive with `chunksize`.
            chunksize: Target rows per partition. Mutually exclusive
                with `npartitions`.
            **kwargs: Forwarded to :meth:`FeatureCollection.read_file`.
                Filter kwargs (`bbox` / `mask` / `rows` /
                `columns` / `where` / `layer`) are rejected
                because dask-geopandas has no pushdown for them.

        Returns:
            LazyFeatureCollection: A new lazy FC.

        Examples:
            - Read a small GeoJSON as a lazy FC via the classmethod:
                ```python
                >>> import tempfile
                >>> from pathlib import Path
                >>> import geopandas as gpd
                >>> from shapely.geometry import Point
                >>> from pyramids.feature import LazyFeatureCollection
                >>> gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                ...     {"v": [1, 2, 3]},
                ...     geometry=[Point(i, i) for i in range(3)],
                ...     crs="EPSG:4326",
                ... )
                >>> d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
                >>> p = d / "pts.geojson"
                >>> gdf.to_file(p, driver="GeoJSON")
                >>> lfc = LazyFeatureCollection.read_file(str(p), npartitions=1)
                >>> lfc.npartitions
                1
                >>> len(lfc.compute())
                3

                ```
        """
        from pyramids.feature import FeatureCollection

        result = FeatureCollection.read_file(
            path,
            backend="dask",
            npartitions=npartitions,
            chunksize=chunksize,
            **kwargs,
        )
        return result

    @property
    def epsg(self) -> int | None:
        """EPSG code of the CRS, or `None` when the CRS is unset.

        Cheap — reads the cached pyproj CRS attached to the
        dask-geopandas frame and calls `.to_epsg()`. No graph
        materialisation.

        Examples:
            - Inspect the EPSG of a lazy FC built from a WGS84 GDF:
                ```python
                >>> import geopandas as gpd
                >>> import dask_geopandas as dg
                >>> from shapely.geometry import Point
                >>> from pyramids.feature import LazyFeatureCollection
                >>> gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                ...     {"v": [1]},
                ...     geometry=[Point(0, 0)],
                ...     crs="EPSG:4326",
                ... )
                >>> lfc = LazyFeatureCollection.from_dask_gdf(
                ...     dg.from_geopandas(gdf, npartitions=1)
                ... )
                >>> lfc.epsg
                4326

                ```
        """
        crs = self.crs
        result = None if crs is None else crs.to_epsg()
        return result

    def compute_total_bounds(self) -> Any:
        """Materialise :attr:`total_bounds` via an explicit `.compute()` call.

        :attr:`total_bounds` on a
        :class:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame` is a lazy dask Scalar.
        Most consumers who want concrete numbers today wrote
        `lfc.total_bounds.compute()` — this helper gives them a
        single-line, self-documenting equivalent that also makes the
        compute-cost explicit in the method name.

        Returns:
            numpy.ndarray: `[minx, miny, maxx, maxy]` as a
            4-element 1-D array — the exact shape
            :class:`geopandas.GeoDataFrame.total_bounds` returns.

        Examples:
            - Force the reduction and destructure into named values:
                ```python
                >>> import geopandas as gpd
                >>> import dask_geopandas as dg
                >>> from shapely.geometry import Point
                >>> from pyramids.feature import LazyFeatureCollection
                >>> gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                ...     {"v": [1, 2]},
                ...     geometry=[Point(0, 0), Point(10, 20)],
                ...     crs="EPSG:4326",
                ... )
                >>> lfc = LazyFeatureCollection.from_dask_gdf(
                ...     dg.from_geopandas(gdf, npartitions=1)
                ... )
                >>> xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = lfc.compute_total_bounds()
                >>> float(xmin), float(ymax)
                (0.0, 20.0)

                ```
        """
        return self.total_bounds.compute()

    def plot(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """No lazy plot path; materialize first.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: Always. Call `.compute().plot(...)` to
                materialize before plotting.

        Examples:
            - Calling `.plot` directly raises with an actionable hint:
                ```python
                >>> import geopandas as gpd
                >>> import dask_geopandas as dg
                >>> from shapely.geometry import Point
                >>> from pyramids.feature import LazyFeatureCollection
                >>> gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                ...     {"v": [1]},
                ...     geometry=[Point(0, 0)],
                ...     crs="EPSG:4326",
                ... )
                >>> lfc = LazyFeatureCollection.from_dask_gdf(
                ...     dg.from_geopandas(gdf, npartitions=1)
                ... )
                >>> try:
                ...     lfc.plot()
                ... except NotImplementedError as exc:
                ...     "compute().plot" in str(exc)
                True

                ```
        """
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "LazyFeatureCollection.plot is not supported — call "
            ".compute().plot(...) to materialize first."
        )

    def compute(self, **kwargs: Any) -> FeatureCollection:
        """Materialize the graph and return an eager :class:`FeatureCollection`.

        The `from pyramids.feature import FeatureCollection`
        import below is inline by necessity — `collection.py` imports
        this module from inside its dask branch, so a top-of-file import
        here would form a cycle. Per `CLAUDE.md`, circular-import
        breaks are the second accepted exception to the no-inline-imports
        rule.

        Args:
            **kwargs: Forwarded to
                :meth:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame.compute` (e.g.
                `scheduler="processes"`).

        Returns:
            FeatureCollection: an eager wrapper around the materialized
            :class:`geopandas.GeoDataFrame`.

        Examples:
            - Compute a two-partition lazy frame back to eager form:
                ```python
                >>> import geopandas as gpd
                >>> import dask_geopandas as dg
                >>> from shapely.geometry import Point
                >>> from pyramids.feature import (
                ...     FeatureCollection, LazyFeatureCollection,
                ... )
                >>> gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                ...     {"v": [1, 2, 3, 4]},
                ...     geometry=[Point(i, i) for i in range(4)],
                ...     crs="EPSG:4326",
                ... )
                >>> lfc = LazyFeatureCollection.from_dask_gdf(
                ...     dg.from_geopandas(gdf, npartitions=2)
                ... )
                >>> eager = lfc.compute()
                >>> len(eager)
                4
                >>> eager.epsg
                4326

                ```
        """
        from pyramids.feature import FeatureCollection

        gdf = super().compute(**kwargs)
        result = FeatureCollection(gdf)
        return result

    def persist(self, **kwargs: Any) -> LazyFeatureCollection:
        """Persist partitions in worker memory; keep the FC lazy.

        Args:
            **kwargs: Forwarded to
                :meth:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame.persist`.

        Returns:
            LazyFeatureCollection: A new lazy FC whose graph has been
            materialized into worker memory.

        Examples:
            - Persist and confirm the result is still lazy:
                ```python
                >>> import geopandas as gpd
                >>> import dask_geopandas as dg
                >>> from shapely.geometry import Point
                >>> from pyramids.feature import LazyFeatureCollection
                >>> gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                ...     {"v": [1, 2]},
                ...     geometry=[Point(0, 0), Point(1, 1)],
                ...     crs="EPSG:4326",
                ... )
                >>> lfc = LazyFeatureCollection.from_dask_gdf(
                ...     dg.from_geopandas(gdf, npartitions=2)
                ... )
                >>> persisted = lfc.persist()
                >>> isinstance(persisted, LazyFeatureCollection)
                True
                >>> persisted.npartitions
                2

                ```
        """
        persisted = super().persist(**kwargs)
        result = type(self).from_dask_gdf(persisted)
        return result

    def spatial_shuffle(
        self,
        by: str = "hilbert",
        level: int = 16,
        *,
        npartitions: int | None = None,
        divisions: Any = None,
    ) -> LazyFeatureCollection:
        """Spatially sort rows via a space-filling curve.

        Thin override of :meth:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame.spatial_shuffle`
        that rewraps the result as a :class:`LazyFeatureCollection`.
        Populates :attr:`spatial_partitions`, enabling partition-pruned
        :meth:`sjoin` on the result.

        Args:
            by: One of `"hilbert"`, `"morton"`, or `"geohash"`.
            level: Curve resolution; default 16.

                ```python
                ...     lfc.to_file("out.geojson")
                ... except NotImplementedError as exc:
                ...     "compute().to_file" in str(exc)
                ```

            "LazyFeatureCollection.to_file is not supported — "
            "dask-geopandas has no lazy OGR write path. Call "
            ".compute().to_file(path) to materialize first, or "

    def to_parquet(self, path: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """Write the lazy frame to GeoParquet (the one genuinely-lazy writer).

        explicit wrapper around
        :meth:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame.to_parquet`. The parent
        returns a :class:`dask.delayed.Delayed` (or `None` when the
        call is implicitly computed), which leaks the dask detail into
        user code and breaks the pyramids convention that `to_*`
        writers return `None`. This override normalises the contract:

        * The call blocks until every partition has been written.
        * Return is always `None` — matches
          :meth:`FeatureCollection.to_parquet` and
          :meth:`LazyFeatureCollection.to_file` (the raising stub).
        * All other kwargs (`compression=`, `write_index=`,
          `storage_options=`) forward to the parent.

        Args:
            path: Destination path or directory. Cloud URLs (`s3://`,
                `gs://`, `az://`) work via `storage_options`.
            *args: Forwarded to
                :meth:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame.to_parquet`.
            **kwargs: Forwarded to
                :meth:`dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame.to_parquet`.
                `compute=True` is forced; passing `compute=False`
                raises :class:`ValueError` because the pyramids API
                contract is "`to_*` always writes, never defers".

            ValueError: If `compute=False` is supplied. Use the
                parent's API directly if you need a Delayed.

                ```python
                >>> import tempfile  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> from pathlib import Path  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> import geopandas as gpd  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> import dask_geopandas as dg  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> from shapely.geometry import Point  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> from pyramids.feature import LazyFeatureCollection  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                ...     {"id": [1, 2]},
                ...     geometry=[Point(0, 0), Point(1, 1)],
                ...     crs="EPSG:4326",
                ... )  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> lfc = LazyFeatureCollection.from_dask_gdf(
                ...     dg.from_geopandas(gdf, npartitions=1)
                ... )  # doctest: +SKIP
                >>> lfc.to_parquet(d / "out.parquet")  # doctest: +SKIP

                ```
        """
        if kwargs.get("compute") is False:
            raise ValueError(
                "LazyFeatureCollection.to_parquet always writes — "
                "passing compute=False is not supported. Use "
                "self._data.to_parquet(...) or go through the "
                "dask_geopandas parent API directly if you need a "
                "Delayed."
            )
        kwargs["compute"] = True
        # dask_geopandas writes through fsspec, which resolves the scheme itself
        # and does not register every spelling GDAL accepts (#918).
        super().to_parquet(to_fsspec_url(str(path)), *args, **kwargs)

        """Pyramids-branded repr; avoids the generic Dask DataFrame one."""
        return (
            f"LazyFeatureCollection(npartitions={self.npartitions}, "
            f"columns={list(self.columns)}, crs={self.crs})"
        )

Return a class-swapped view of every inherited method's result.

dask-geopandas inherits from dask-expr and does not honour pandas' classic _constructor hook. Methods like to_crs, clip, sjoin, copy, drop_duplicates go through map_partitions with meta inference and produce a plain :class:dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame, silently dropping the :class:LazyFeatureCollection subclass. This hook wraps every public callable so that a :class:dask_geopandas.GeoDataFrame result is rebranded back to the subclass before it reaches the caller. Private names (_-prefixed) are passed through unchanged to keep dask-expr internals — meta inference, name caches, partition probing — on the hot path they expect.
